item: Is TB treatment free?
rule: Answer given: "Yes. Under the National TB Elimination Programme, tests and medicines are free at government health facilities. Patients may also receive money for nutrition support." (from Tuberculosis (TB))

item: Why should I finish my TB medicine?
rule: Answer given: "TB can be cured. Treatment usually takes at least 6 months. It is very important to take every dose and finish the full course, even after you feel better. Stopping early can cause drug-resistant TB, which is much harder to treat." (from Tuberculosis (TB))
sources: No source recorded

item: How does TB spread?
rule: Answer given: "Tuberculosis (TB) is caused by germs that usually attack the lungs, but can affect any part of the body. It spreads through the air when a person with TB of the lungs coughs, sneezes, or talks." (from Tuberculosis (TB))
sources: No source recorded

item: What is TB?
rule: Answer given: "Tuberculosis (TB) is caused by germs that usually attack the lungs, but can affect any part of the body. It spreads through the air when a person with TB of the lungs coughs, sneezes, or talks. TB is a serious infection, but it can be cured with free treatment. A cough lasting more than 2 weeks should always be tested." (from Tuberculosis (TB))
sources: No source recorded

item: How does HIV spread?
rule: Answer given: "Mizoram has the highest rate of HIV among Indian states. Sharing needles while injecting drugs and unprotected sex are the main ways it spreads here. Free testing is available at every district hospital, and free ART treatment is available in the state. HIV does not spread through everyday contact, food, water, or mosquito bites." (from HIV & AIDS)
sources: No source recorded

item: Where can I get an HIV test?
rule: Answer given: "At any Integrated Counselling and Testing Centre (ICTC) in government hospitals. The test is free, quick, and confidential. You can also call 1097 for guidance." (from HIV & AIDS)
sources: No source recorded

item: What is PEP?
rule: Answer given: "PEP (post-exposure prophylaxis) is a short course of medicine taken after a possible exposure to HIV. It must be started within 72 hours — the sooner the better. Ask at a government hospital." (from HIV & AIDS)
sources: No source recorded

item: What is HIV?
rule: Answer given: "HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) attacks the body's defence system. Without treatment, it slowly weakens the body until it cannot fight infections. This late stage is called AIDS. There is no cure yet, but medicine called ART (antiretroviral therapy) keeps HIV under control. People who take ART every day can live a normal lifespan. When the virus is kept very low (undetectable), they do not pass HIV to their partners through sex." (from HIV & AIDS)
sources: No source recorded

item: What does blood pressure mean?
rule: Answer given: "The top number is the pressure when your heart beats; the bottom number is when it rests. Below 120/80 is normal. 140/90 or above usually means high blood pressure and needs a doctor's advice. High blood pressure is called the 'silent killer' because it usually has no symptoms. The only way to know your blood pressure is to check it." (from Heart Health)
sources: No source recorded

item: What is a heart attack?
rule: Answer given: "A heart attack happens when blood flow to part of the heart is blocked. A stroke happens when blood flow to part of the brain is blocked or a blood vessel bursts. Both are emergencies — every minute counts." (from Heart Health)
sources: No source recorded

item: Can I take painkillers for dengue?
rule: Answer given: "Do not take aspirin or ibuprofen if dengue is possible — they can increase bleeding. Ask a doctor what is safe, rest, and drink plenty of fluids." (from Malaria & Dengue)

item: What is dengue?
rule: Answer given: "Dengue is caused by a virus carried by Aedes mosquitoes, which breed in clean water collected in containers, tyres, and pots. Most people recover, but some develop severe dengue with bleeding and shock." (from Malaria & Dengue)

item: Where can I get a malaria test?
rule: Answer given: "At any government health centre, and from ASHAs in many villages using a rapid test. Testing and treatment are free." (from Malaria & Dengue)
sources: No source recorded

item: What is malaria?
rule: Answer given: "Malaria is caused by a parasite carried by Anopheles mosquitoes. It causes fever with chills and can become severe within a day, especially in children and pregnant women. Malaria can be cured if treated early. Any fever during the rainy season should be tested. A quick blood test can tell if it is malaria." (from Malaria & Dengue)
sources: No source recorded

item: What is diabetes?
rule: Answer given: "When you eat, your body turns food into sugar (glucose) for energy. A hormone called insulin helps sugar move from the blood into your cells. In diabetes, the body does not make enough insulin or cannot use it well, so sugar builds up in the blood." (from Diabetes Awareness)
sources: No source recorded
